Initial FAST processing was carried out using 10 g of the alloy powder blend to produce 20 mm diameter samples.
After milling and FAST consolidation, the microstructure changed considerably. The FAST microstructure appeared more homogeneous and refined
An Arcast Arc 200 arc melter with non-consumable tungsten electrode was used to melt the elements together in a water cooled copper crucible.
The ingots were initially crushed using a percussion mortar.
The crushed particulate material was then placed into a zirconia-lined jar, along with zirconia grinding balls, fitted with an aeration lid and flushed with argon to create an inert atmosphere.
The powder was sieved to < 250 μ m and the resulting particle size distribution (PSD) was measured by laser diffraction using a Malvern Mastersizer 3000.
The sample was heated at 150 °C min 1 up to 1300 °C, then at 75 °C min 1 to a maximum temperature of 1500 °C, at which point a pressure of 50 MPa was applied and held for 5 min.

The microstructure of the FAST alloy, which is comprised of bcc Nbss and tetragonal α Nb5Si3 was more homogenous compared with the cast alloy, with some interstitial contamination that occurred during powder production.
After FAST, the stable phases were bcc Nbss and the low temperature stable α Nb5Si3 silicide.
